source:
Speaker A: The policy should call AI grammar rewriting plagiarism when the tool changes sentences students submit as their own.
Speaker B: That is not plagiarism. Plagiarism is taking someone else's ideas or words without credit; cleaning awkward phrasing is closer to using a tutor.
Speaker A: If the submitted wording is generated by the system, the student is misrepresenting authorship.
Speaker B: Authorship of ideas is what matters for this assignment, not whether a tool smoothed the wording.

extraction.mainQuestion: Does AI grammar rewriting count as plagiarism for the assignment?

positions.label: Generated wording is plagiarism
positions.thesis: AI grammar rewriting should count as plagiarism when it changes the wording students submit as their own.
positions.steelman: If the submitted wording comes from the system, the student is misrepresenting authorship of the text.

groundingQuotes.quote: The policy should call AI grammar rewriting plagiarism

positions.label: Plagiarism requires borrowed ideas or words
positions.thesis: AI grammar rewriting is not plagiarism if it only smooths phrasing and the student's ideas remain their own.
positions.steelman: The assignment should treat plagiarism as unattributed borrowing of ideas or words, not ordinary wording help.

resolution.condition: The course must define whether authorship covers wording, ideas, or both.

claims.statement: For this assignment, plagiarism turns on authorship of ideas rather than tool-smoothed wording.

resolution.condition: The course must stipulate what counts as plagiarism in tool-assisted writing.

groundingQuotes.quote: Authorship of ideas is what matters for this assignment

disagreementCandidates.question: Does plagiarism include AI-generated wording when the ideas are still the student's?
disagreementCandidates.summary: They use different definitions of plagiarism in the AI grammar context.

participantStances.stance: No, plagiarism requires borrowed ideas or words.

disagreementCandidates.resolutionCondition: Stipulate whether the policy treats wording authorship as part of plagiarism.

caveats: The transcript uses anonymous speaker labels, so no personal identity is inferred.
